source.title: The hippocampal-VTA loop: controlling the entry of information into long-term memory.

confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily-cited mechanistic review that directly establishes a novelty-gated write into long-term memory -- the exact function of the MECH-189 WRITE gate. Strongly supports the existence of gate (b) as a real biological control point. Counts as 'mixed' rather than 'supports' for the operationalisation question because the biology it describes diverges from the self-contained novelty-vs-anchors proxy in two ways: (i) the novelty signal is a hippocampal comparator mismatch against the FULL long-term store, not against a small goal-anchor subset; (ii) VTA firing (and hence the dopaminergic plasticity gate) is an explicit CONJUNCTION of novelty WITH salience and goal information, so complexity and salience are not orthogonal channels. | 2026-06-24 tag-join: DEV-NEED-006 (the developmental WRITE-gate sub-need of MECH-189 -- high-salience benefit contact written to a durable super-ordinal goal anchor) added to claim_ids_tested. This paper evidences that WRITE gate as faithfully as it does MECH-189; the addition joins existing prior art to the DEV-NEED-006 experiment tag (v3_exq_588e) and clears a false novel_discovery quadrant flag that arose only because the experiment was tagged to the gate id while the literature was tagged to the parent claim.
failure_signatures: If the write gate measures novelty only against the goal-anchor set (super_ordinal_complexity_mode='novelty'), it computes mismatch against the wrong reference: the biological comparator detects information 'not already stored in long-term memory', i.e. mismatch against the whole stored model.

Treating salience (gate a) and complexity/novelty (gate b) as independent multiplicands departs from the biology, where the same VTA dopaminergic signal integrates novelty, salience, and goal information into a single gate.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The hippocampus detects newly arrived information not already in long-term memory; the resulting novelty signal travels via subiculum -> accumbens -> ventral pallidum -> VTA, where it combines with salience and goal information to drive dopaminergic firing; dopamine released back into hippocampus enhances LTP and learning, thereby regulating entry of information into long-term memory.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the biological template for the MECH-189 WRITE gate: a high-salience benefit contact is written to persistent ContextMemory only when a novelty/complexity signal licenses it. The hippocampal-VTA loop validates that a novelty-gated, dopamine-mediated write into durable memory is real, and that the gate is a conjunction of novelty + salience + goal -- matching MECH-189's 'high salience AND high contextual complexity' conjunction.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The loop computes novelty as comparator mismatch against the entire stored model, whereas the default super_ordinal_complexity_mode='novelty' measures 1 - cosine to the goal-ANCHOR keys only. The reference sets differ, so the proxy is a narrower, possibly biased estimator of the biological novelty signal. The review is also a synthesis/model, not a single direct test of a goal-memory write.
mapping.source_context: Rodent/primate hippocampal-midbrain circuit; conceptual review with electrophysiological and lesion support.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (foundational Neuron review). Mapping fidelity good for the gate concept but only moderate for the specific 'novelty-vs-own-anchors' operationalisation, since the biological reference set is the full LTM. Transfer risk moderate: animal circuit -> abstract REE z_world/z_goal store.
